findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_hotels" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search hotel properties in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, the United Kingdom and the United States, and price them for a stay in the same call. ASK BEFORE YOU S…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "list_hotels" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_hotels" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_hotels · Public sink: list_hotels.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_hotels · Public sink: list_hotels

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
